title: Missing rule for rmarkdown compatibility ?
description:
**rmarkdown** adds specific rule when using bootstrap. They are not part of **bslib** and are adding inside **rmarkdown**

We may need to add them 

````r
  # Boostrap with bslib package
  if (is_bs_theme(theme)) {
    # TODO: would it make sense for these additional rules to come as a part of
    # bslib::bs_theme_dependencies() (for consistency sake)?
    h1_size <- if ("3" %in% theme_version(theme)) "font-size-h1" else "h1-font-size"
    theme <- bslib::bs_add_rules(
      theme, c(
        paste0("h1.title {margin-top: 1.25rem; font-size: 1.15 * $", h1_size, "}"),
        "pre:not([class]) { background-color: $body-bg }"
      )
    )
    return(bslib::bs_theme_dependencies(theme))
  }
````

title: Conflict with bslib
description:
Currently this assumes that we use bslib to activate bootstrap version 4 and we just replace the bootstrap dependency with the one from rstrap.

However **bslib** also adds other dependency - one being `bs3compat`

Currently the order of dependency cause this issue
```js
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'Constructor' of undefined
    at bs3compat.js:11
    at bs3compat.js:44
```

This is because rstrap will not replace bootstrap files from bslib but will be loaded as a new dependency with same name but higher version **after** the bslib one. This cause a failure due to order of dependency. 

We need to remove b3compat or change the order.

Note: bslib will load bootstrap.bundle.js and not just bootstrap.js - not sure if that matters.
